shared_elements: low-relief carving on weathered pale/tan stone
horizontal band or register of repeated small motifs
animal figures in profile (bird-like and quadruped forms)
blue sky visible above the carved surface
outdoor in-situ stone surface with damaged/eroded areas
justification: Both show weathered tan stone carved in low relief against open sky, and each includes a horizontal band of small, evenly repeated motifs plus profile animal shapes and disc forms. But A is an essentially uniform, flat wall of dense, tiny, shallow-incised signs filling every register, whereas B is a free-standing block dominated by a few large, boldly modelled raised animal figures with much empty ground, so the scale, relief depth and compositional logic are quite different.
